1.title: Preparing Artifacts and Configuration
1.text: Welcome to Module eleven: Preparing Artifacts and Configuration. It covers the exam area Domain three: Testing and Deployment. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Manage dependencies for code modules within packages (three point one.one). Build and manage container images (three point one.two). Use code repositories in deployment environments (three point one.three). Manage environment-specific application configuration (three point one.four). Use A P I Gateway features and resources such as stage-specific U R Ls and endpoints (three point one.five). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Domain three: Testing and Deployment (twenty-two percent). Exam format: fifty scored questions, multiple choice and multiple response; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A W S Developer Associate (D V A-C three) exam guide.

1.title: Packaging code
1.text: Packaging code. Lambda zip. Code plus dependencies in a dot zip; layers share common dependencies. Lambda container image. Up to ten gigabytes, built from a Dockerfile, stored in Amazon E C R. Application bundle. For E C two or on-premises deploys, a bundle with an App Spec file (Module thirteen). Dependencies. Pin versions, package them with the code, keep the package small to deploy and start faster.

1.title: Container images and Amazon ECR
1.text: Container images and Amazon E C R. The figure shows this: Build an image, tag it, push it to E C R, and deploy it to Lambda, E C S or E K S.

1.title: Container images and Amazon ECR, continued
1.text: Container images and Amazon E C R. Dockerfile. The recipe that builds the image. Amazon E C R. Managed container registry. Image tag. A label such as v one dot four or prod; immutable tags stop overwriting. Lifecycle policy. Rules that expire old or untagged images to save space. Image scanning. Finds known vulnerabilities in images. Authentication. Get a token with aws ecr get login password, then docker login and docker push. Exam tip: "Remove untagged and old images automatically" equals E C R lifecycle policy. "Do not allow a tag to be overwritten" equals immutable tags.

1.title: Code repositories
1.text: Code repositories. Deployments pull code from a version-controlled repository (for example Git Hub or another Git service); Code Pipeline and Code Build can start from repository events. Use branches for environments and tags for releases (Module thirteen).

1.title: Environment-specific configuration
1.text: Environment-specific configuration. A W S App Config. Feature flags and runtime configuration with validation and gradual rollout with rollback. Systems Manager Parameter Store. Configuration values and simple secrets, organized by path (for example slash app slash prod slash db ). A W S Secrets Manager. Secrets with rotation. Lambda environment variables. Small, non-secret settings per function or alias. A P I Gateway stage variables. Values per stage (for example the Lambda alias to call). Exam tip: Change a setting without redeploying, roll it out gradually equals App Config. Keep one codebase and vary the settings per environment.

1.title: API Gateway stages and endpoints
1.text: A P I Gateway stages and endpoints. Stage. A named deployment of an A P I (dev, test, prod); each has its own U R L (... slash dev,... slash prod ). Stage variables. Per-stage settings. Canary release. Send a percentage of traffic to a new deployment on a stage. Custom domain name. Map your own domain to an A P I stage. Endpoint types. Edge-optimized, Regional, Private (inside a V P C). Exam tip: One codebase, many environments: stages, aliases and per-environment parameters, not copies of the code.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Old and untagged container images are filling an E C R repository. What should the team add? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A lifecycle policy. Lifecycle policies expire images automatically.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A team wants feature flags that can be changed without redeploying and rolled out gradually. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A W S App Config. App Config supports validated, gradual configuration rollouts.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A developer wants each environment of an A P I to have its own U R L. What should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A P I Gateway stages. Each stage has its own invoke U R L.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A Lambda function needs a large machine-learning library of three gigabytes. What is the right packaging? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A container image. Container images allow up to ten gigabytes; zip packages are much smaller.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Configuration values for dev, test and prod should share one codebase. Where can the values live? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Parameter Store paths per environment. Path-organized parameters let one codebase read per-environment settings.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A team does not want an image tag overwritten after release. What should be enabled? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Immutable tags. Immutable tags prevent overwriting an existing tag.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the maximum Lambda container image size? Answer: ten gigabytes. Question two. Which registry stores container images on A W S? Answer: Amazon E C R. Question three. What does a stage variable hold? Answer: A per-stage setting for an A P I.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which tool offers validation and gradual rollout of configuration? Answer: A W S App Config. Question five. Name two secret or configuration stores. Answer: Secrets Manager and Parameter Store. Question six. What does an E C R image scan find? Answer: Known vulnerabilities in the image.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Packages: zip plus layers; container image up to ten gigabytes in E C R. E C R: tags, immutable tags, lifecycle policies, scanning. Config: App Config (flags, rollout), Parameter Store, Secrets Manager, env vars. A P I Gateway: stages with own U R Ls, stage variables, canary, custom domains.
